messages:
Maya (Support): Grace from Acme reports a spike of 502s for hosted API in us-east-1 starting ~10:20 UTC. Says errors started right after your cert rotation earlier today. Example curl: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate` -> TLS handshake timeout on client side.

Grace (Customer): yup, we started seeing 502/504s for ~15-30s bursts then it recovers. Our ops recorded `TLS handshake timed out` in our client logs. Happened across multiple machines. We can share pcap if needed.

Maya (Support): thanks. I've queued this as P2. tagging @Ravi and @Jon — can you triage if this looks like cert rotation fallout vs resolver issues?

Ravi (SRE): looking. two quick checks: 1) cert rotation finished at 10:15 UTC per deploy-bot, 2) our edge telemetry shows a short-lived increase in handshake timeouts at 10:18-10:23 in us-east-1. attaching quick trace extract below.

Ravi (SRE): ```
# edge-handshake-trace
time window: 10:16-10:25 UTC
region: us-east-1
handshake_timeouts: +420% (baseline)
primary-cause: TLS client aborts during handshake (ClientHello->no response)
```

Jon (Network): hmm could be upstream resolver returning stale CNAME for some POPs. I see a pattern where a subset of resolver IPs returned the old cert-serving hostname that had no matching cert chain after rotation. Can @dns-bot dump recent resolver responses?

dns-bot: dump complete. sample outputs:
- resolver 10.3.12.45 -> `api.redwood.example.com CNAME edge-us-east.old.example.net` TTL 3600 (stale)
- resolver 10.4.77.12 -> `api.redwood.example.com CNAME edge-us-east.new.example.net` TTL 60

Ravi (SRE): that TTL mismatch is suspicious — some resolvers still holding the old CNAME with high TTL so clients hit a backend that wasn't serving the rotated cert. That would cause handshake aborts when SNI/cert mismatch occurs.

Grace (Customer): we saw different error strings depending on the client runtime: some got `certificate_verify_failed`, others got `handshake timeout`.

Maya (Support): copying a repro checklist for SRE/network to run against customer's environment: 1) from a failing client host run `dig +trace api.redwood.example.com` and `curl -v` to capture TLS logs; 2) capture full tcpdump during a failure window; 3) check local resolver cache TTLs (`systemd-resolve --statistics` or `nslookup`); 4) confirm which resolver IPs the customer uses.

Ravi (SRE): running remote checks against sample IPs Grace provided. `dig api.redwood.example.com @10.3.12.45` returns CNAME to old edge for ~30% of queries, others return new. Running `openssl s_client -connect <edge-ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com` against the old-edge-ip returns cert chain for `edge-us-east.old.example.net` which does not include the new SAN for `api.redwood.example.com`. So handshake fails.

Jon (Network): root cause hypothesis: certificate rotation included canonical host change (we folded `api.redwood.example.com` behind new-edge hostname) and we added a CNAME change. Some third-party resolvers (or customer resolvers) cached the previous CNAME due to higher TTL on delegation/glue somewhere, causing a split-brain where some clients went to nodes without the updated cert.

Ravi (SRE): mitigation applied: configured per-pop routing fallback to accept both old and new hostnames in us-east for 30m and temporarily increased proxy SNI acceptance to be tolerant of both cert chains while we flush DNS. also triggered an automatic reissue to re-add old SAN to new certs as a stopgap.

deploy-bot: cert-rotation job completed at 10:15 UTC by release/edge-rollout (id: r-2026-04-15). rollback option available.

Jon (Network): longer-term fix: we need to ensure when we change CNAMEs during cert rotations we keep TTLs low ahead of cutover and pre-warm resolver caches, and add a short lived DNS alias stable for 48h. Also add monitoring for per-resolver CNAME variance.

Maya (Support): Grace, can you try this quick test to confirm fix? 1) `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` on one of your failing hosts, 2) `dig @<your-resolver-ip> api.redwood.example.com +short any` and post results, 3) `curl -v` again.

Grace (Customer): flushed, dig now returns `edge-us-east.new.example.net` consistently, curl succeeding now. We still saw intermittent fails on a few hosts but much reduced. Thanks for the quick mitigation.

Ravi (SRE): note — we'll keep fallback in place and rollback guard for another hour while we watch telemetry. We'll also open a followup to change our rotation playbook: pre-lower TTL to 60s 2 hours pre-rotation, add canary for resolver variance, and avoid removing old SANs until 24h after cutover.

Maya (Support): tagging incident followup owner — @Ravi please create postmortem and add customer impact timeline so we can offer credit if needed.

Ravi (SRE): on it. preliminary RCA: DNS CNAME TTL mismatch + cert SAN rotation -> splitter resolver behavior -> handshake failures -> transient 502s/504s. Action items: DNS prewarm, playbook updates, add metric for per-resolver CNAME drift.

Grace (Customer): thanks everyone, we'll monitor. appreciate the speedy response :thumbsup:

Maya (Support): closing thread when postmortem is filed. if anything else shows up @Grace just re-open.
